batch69_inventory_mirrors.statement:
Use the dual-number scheme, relative projective-space charts, finite locally free sheaves and twisting sheaves in [[def-dual-numbers-scheme]], [[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]], [[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]] and [[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]], with the inherited AC convention for the twisting-sheaf construction. Let $A=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ and equip it with the conjugate-linear involution $\overline{a+b\epsilon}=\bar a+\bar b\epsilon$. Its reduction is the quotient map $A\to\mathbb C$ sending $\epsilon$ to zero. For every $r\in\mathbb R$, the map $\rho_r:A\to A$ fixing $\mathbb C$ and sending $\epsilon$ to $r\epsilon$ preserves this involution.

A **first-order family of positive real linear monads of dimensions $(k,2k+N,k)$** is a three-term complex of locally free sheaves on $\mathbb P^3_A=\operatorname{Proj}A[\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2]$,
$$\mathcal O(-1)\otimes_A U_A\xrightarrow{\alpha_A}\mathcal O\otimes_A S_A\xrightarrow{\beta_A}\mathcal O(1)\otimes_A U'_A,$$
where $U_A,S_A,U'_A$ are free $A$-modules of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, each map is homogeneous linear in $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)$, $\beta_A\alpha_A=0$, $\alpha_A$ is a locally split injection, $\beta_A$ is a locally split surjection, and $F_A=\ker\beta_A/\operatorname{im}\alpha_A$ is locally free of rank $N$. The two short exact sequences defined by the kernel and image split locally; hence their formation and the middle cohomology commute with reduction $A\to\mathbb C$. The reduced complex is therefore an ordinary linear monad on $\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C$.

The **first-order locally-free/base-change range** used here further requires that $H^0(\mathbb P^3_A,F_A)$ is a free $A$-module and reduction identifies it with $H^0(\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C,F_0)$, where $F_0=F_A\otimes_A\mathbb C$. The image in $S_A$ of the map from the four coefficient copies of $U_A$ under $\alpha_A$ is a direct summand and reduces to the corresponding coefficient-image subspace of $S_0$. For each real twistor line $\ell$ in the reduced projective space, the restriction of $F_A$ to $\ell_A=\ell\times_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Spec}A$ is trivial of rank $N$, and reduction identifies its global sections with $H^0(\ell,F_0|_\ell)$. These conditions state the precise global, coefficient-image, and line-section base-change range; no arbitrary analytic family or algebraization assertion is included.

Extend the coordinate map $j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$ semilinearly using the involution of $A$; its projective action $\sigma$ is an involution and preserves each real twistor line. A **real twistor line** means the projectivization of a $j$-invariant complex two-plane in $\mathbb C^4$. Equivalently these are the finite lines
$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,\qquad (z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2,$$
together with $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Indeed a nonzero vector $v$ and $jv$ are complex-linearly independent because $j^2=-1$; they span the invariant plane. If its $\lambda$ projection is nonzero, that projection and its quaternionic conjugate give an invertible two-by-two matrix with determinant $|\lambda_1|^2+|\lambda_2|^2$, so it has exactly the displayed graph form; if the projection is zero the plane is the $\mu$ plane. Each fixed-line restriction above means the corresponding constant thickening $\ell_A$.

A first-order real structure on the monad is a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian pairing on $F_A$, linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, whose reduction induces a positive-definite Hermitian form on the holomorphic section space of every real line. A unitary framing at infinity is an isometric isomorphism $F_A|_{\ell_\infty}\cong (A\otimes_\mathbb C W)\otimes_A\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$, where $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ has its standard Hermitian form.

An isomorphism of such families is an $A$-linear chain isomorphism that intertwines the $\sigma$-Hermitian pairings and the framing. No order or positivity is assigned to elements of $A$ with nonzero nilpotent part: positivity is required only after reduction. The base-change scope in this definition consists exactly of reduction $\epsilon\mapsto0$ and the involution-preserving maps $\rho_r$ for real $r$.

batch69_inventory_mirrors.statement: Let $M$ be the coefficient-image subspace of a linear monad on $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ after removing its constant orthogonal summand as in the preceding splitting lemma. Thus its reduced middle cohomology has no global sections, is trivial on every $\sigma$-invariant real line, and has a positive section pairing on each such line. Let $H$ be the induced nondegenerate Hermitian form on $M$, linear in the first variable, and suppose $\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H$ and $\beta(z)\alpha(z)=0$ for every $z\in\mathbb C^4$, with $j^2=-1$. Then $H$ is positive definite on all of $M$.

batch69_inventory_mirrors.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $k\ge0$ and
$N\ge2$. On $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ with homogeneous coordinates
$(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)$, set
$$j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2) =(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1), \qquad \sigma([z])=[jz].$$
For each $(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$, let $\ell_z$ be the real twistor line
defined by
$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,$$
and let $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Suppose
$$\mathcal O(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{\alpha} \mathcal O\otimes S\xrightarrow{\beta} \mathcal O(1)\otimes U'$$
is a complex of holomorphic vector bundles with $\beta\alpha=0$, locally split
injective and surjective end maps, and locally free middle cohomology
$F=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ of rank $N$, where
$\dim_\mathbb C U=\dim_\mathbb C U'=k$ and
$\dim_\mathbb C S=2k+N$. Suppose $F|_{\ell_z}$ is holomorphically trivial for
every $z$, and it has a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian pairing
whose induced first-slot-linear Hermitian form on
$H^0(\ell_z,F|_{\ell_z})$ is positive definite for every $z$. Here the
pairing means an isomorphism $h:F\to D(F)$ fixed by $D$, where for a
homogeneous linear matrix $P$ one sets $P^\#(z)=P(jz)^\dagger$ and the signed
dual monad has differentials $-\beta^\#$ and $\alpha^\#$; thus $D^2$ is the
identity under the induced double-dual identifications. Suppose also that a
unitary framing identifies $F|_{\ell_\infty}$ isometrically with
$W\otimes\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$ for a fixed Hermitian space $W$ of dimension
$N$.

Then there are Hermitian
spaces $V$ and $W$ of dimensions $k$ and $N$, with $W$ carrying the prescribed
framing, and maps
$$B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V),\qquad I:W\to V,\qquad J:V\to W$$
such that, after a pairing-preserving framed chain identification, the monad
maps are
$$\alpha= \begin{pmatrix} A\\ C\\ J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \beta=(-C,\ A,\ I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2),$$
where
$$A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1,\qquad C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2.$$
The extracted maps satisfy both zero-moment equations
$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0.$$
They are stable, meaning the vectors
$B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$, and costable, meaning no nonzero
subspace invariant under both $B_i$ is contained in $\ker J$. Conversely,
every such regular datum with both moments zero gives a locally split monad
with the stated real-line positivity and infinity framing.
Here $\dagger$ denotes adjoint in the indicated Hermitian spaces.

In the next assertion, a normalized framed isomorphism is a chain
isomorphism preserving the lifted pairing and the specified infinity frame.
Such isomorphisms correspond exactly to the simultaneous $U(V)$ action
$$(B_1,B_2,I,J)\longmapsto (gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1}),\qquad g\in U(V).$$
Thus inverse coefficient extraction recovers precisely one $U(V)$ orbit; when
$k=0$, $U(0)$ is trivial, and every constant flat summand is retained as an
unused orthogonal subspace of $W$.

For $t_1,t_2\in U(1)$, choose an orthonormal framed basis
$w_1,\ldots,w_N$ of $W$ and phases $e_1,\ldots,e_N\in U(1)$, and let
$h(w_a)=e_a^{-1}w_a$. The coordinate action
$(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto
(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ acts on data by
$$(B_1,B_2,I,J)\mapsto (t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ).$$
The corresponding chain factors on the source, middle and target terms are,
respectively,
$(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$, and $1$.

The same extraction and classification hold naturally for first-order
families over $A=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with
$\bar\epsilon=\epsilon$ in the following exact locally-free/base-change
range: the three modules are free of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, the end maps are
locally split, the middle cohomology is locally free and commutes with
reduction, its global section module is free and commutes with reduction, the
coefficient-image submodule in the middle term is a direct summand and
commutes with reduction, and each fixed real-line restriction is trivial
with its section module commuting with reduction. The framing and pairing
are defined over $A$, while positivity is required only on the reduced
complex; adjoints on these modules use the coefficient involution and the
induced $A$-Hermitian forms. Call an $A$-valued datum regular when its
reduction is stable and costable. The extracted matrices lie over $A$ and
obey the same moment equations. Conversely, every $A$-valued regular datum
whose raw
monad satisfies these same global-section, coefficient-image and real-line
base-change conditions gives a family in this range. Pairing-preserving
framed family isomorphisms correspond exactly to
$U(k,A)=\{g:g^\dagger g=1\}$. This assertion is restricted to reduction and
the involution-preserving base maps $\epsilon\mapsto r\epsilon$ with
$r\in\mathbb R$.

For the finite algebraic monad resolution, let
$H_{\rm alg}=c_1^{\rm alg}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$ and
$H_{\rm top}=c_1^{\rm top}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$. The hyperplane cycle
map identifies these classes in their respective theories. Then
$\operatorname{ch}(F)=N-kH_{\rm alg}^2$ and
$c_2^{\rm alg}(F)=kH_{\rm alg}^2$. Its topological line class is the same
$H_{\rm top}$ and $c_2^{\rm top}(F)=kH_{\rm top}^2$. Identify
$\mathbb P^3$ with the twistor space of $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ through
the quaternionic structure whose invariant lines are the $\ell_z$ and
$\ell_\infty$, and let $\pi:\mathbb P^3\to S^4$ be its projection. Give each
fiber its complex orientation, orient $S^4$ so that the positive incidence
chart followed by the fiber orientation is the complex orientation of
$\mathbb P^3$, and let $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ be the positive point class.
For this positive twistor orientation, $\pi^*u=H_{\rm top}^2$; consequently, if the underlying
topological bundle is $\pi^*E$ for a bundle $E\to S^4$ with $c_1(E)=0$, then
$c_2(E)=ku$.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let
$$
\mathcal O(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal O\otimes S\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal O(1)\otimes U'
$$
be a locally split linear monad on $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ with locally free middle cohomology $F$. Suppose a nondegenerate Hermitian form $H$ on $S$, linear in the first variable, satisfies $\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H$ for $j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. Assume $H^0(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$, $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ for every $q\ge0$, and $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(-1))=0$. Define $L=\bigcap_i\ker\beta_i\subseteq S$ and $M=\sum_i\operatorname{im}\alpha_i\subseteq S$, where $\alpha(z)=\sum_i z_i\alpha_i$ and $\beta(z)=\sum_i z_i\beta_i$. If the Hermitian form induced by $H$ on $H^0(F|_\ell)$ is positive definite for every $\sigma$-invariant real line $\ell$, then $H^0(F)=L=M^{\perp_H}$, $H|_L$ is positive definite, and $S=L\oplus M$ is an $H$-orthogonal decomposition. The monad and its pairing split as the constant summand $L\otimes\mathcal O$ plus the reduced monad $U\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to M\otimes\mathcal O\to U'\otimes\mathcal O(1)$; the reduced cohomology has no global sections and remains positive on every real line. The conclusion includes $U=0$, when $L=S$ and $M=0$.

Assume full AC. Then the analytic sheaf cohomology of $\mathcal O(-1)$ vanishes in every degree on $\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$ for $1\le r\le3$. The analytic cohomology of $\mathcal O(-2)$ vanishes in every degree on $\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$ for $r=2,3$. In particular, $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ and $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-2))=0$ for $q=0,1,2$. This is an analytic deduction from the named scalar-cohomology supplier and does not identify algebraic and analytic cohomology by GAGA.

Let $m\ge1$. A **chart** on a topological space $X$ is a homeomorphism
$\varphi:U\to\varphi(U)$ from an open set $U\subseteq X$ onto an open subset of
$\mathbb C^m$ with its usual topology ([[def-homeomorphism-and-open-maps]]);
two charts $\varphi,\psi$ are **holomorphically compatible** when the
transition maps $\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}$ and $\varphi\circ\psi^{-1}$ are
holomorphic on the open sets where they are defined
([[def-holomorphic-function-in-several-complex-variables]]). A **holomorphic
atlas** is a family of pairwise compatible charts whose domains cover $X$. A
**complex manifold of dimension $m$** is a nonempty Hausdorff
([[def-hausdorff-space]]) second-countable ([[def-second-countable-space]])
topological space carrying a holomorphic atlas; the same maximal-atlas argument
as for [[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]] applies verbatim with
$\mathbb C^m$ in place of $\mathbb C$: the union of a holomorphic atlas with all
charts compatible with it is again a holomorphic atlas, so one passes to the
unique maximal atlas and calls its members holomorphic charts. Each chart is a
homeomorphism onto an open subset of $\mathbb C^m\cong\mathbb R^{2m}$, so $X$ is
a topological manifold without boundary of real dimension $2m$
([[def-topological-manifold-without-boundary]]), and for connected $X$ the case
$m=1$ recovers Riemann surfaces ([[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]]).

A **holomorphic map** $f:X\to Y$ between complex manifolds is a continuous map
whose expression in every pair of holomorphic charts is holomorphic
([[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]]); equivalently, for every open
$V\subseteq Y$ and every holomorphic function $h$ on $V$, the function
$h\circ f$ is holomorphic on $f^{-1}(V)$. The forward implication is the
holomorphic chain rule; conversely apply this condition to the coordinate
functions of a chart on $Y$.

**Induced smooth structure and complex structure.** Holomorphic functions on
open subsets of $\mathbb C^m$ are smooth
([[cor-holomorphic-functions-in-several-variables-are-smooth]]), so every
holomorphic atlas is a smooth atlas ([[def-smooth-atlas]]) and $X$ is a smooth
manifold of real dimension $2m$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]) whose smooth charts
include the holomorphic ones. In holomorphic coordinates
$z_k=x_k+iy_k$ the **complex structure** is the endomorphism field $J$ of the
tangent bundle determined by $J\partial_{x_k}=\partial_{y_k}$ and
$J\partial_{y_k}=-\partial_{x_k}$; it satisfies $J^2=-\mathrm{id}$ and is
independent of the holomorphic chart, because a holomorphic transition map has
complex-linear differential ([[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]],
[[thm-chain-rule-for-holomorphic-maps-in-several-variables]]) and complex-linear
maps intertwine the two coordinate definitions of multiplication by $i$. A
**Hermitian metric** on $X$ is a Riemannian metric $g$
([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]) satisfying
$g(Jv,Jw)=g(v,w)$ for all tangent vectors $v,w$; its Riemannian volume density
is written $\mu_g$ ([[def-riemannian-volume-density]]). The complex structure
makes each tangent space a complex vector space, so the tangent bundle is a
smooth complex vector bundle in the sense of
[[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]].

**Holomorphic vector bundles and Hermitian bundle metrics.** A **holomorphic
vector bundle of rank $r$** on $X$ is a smooth complex vector bundle
$\pi:E\to X$ of rank $r$
([[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]],
[[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]]) together with an open
cover $(V_\alpha)$ of $X$ and smooth local trivializations
$\theta_\alpha:E|_{V_\alpha}\to V_\alpha\times\mathbb C^r$ whose transition
matrices $g_{\alpha\beta}:V_\alpha\cap V_\beta\to\mathrm{GL}_r(\mathbb C)$,
defined by $\theta_\alpha\theta_\beta^{-1}(p,v)=(p,g_{\alpha\beta}(p)v)$, are
holomorphic. A **holomorphic frame** over an open set $V$ is a smooth
complex-linear trivialization whose transition matrices with the supplied
trivializations are holomorphic on every overlap. Changing holomorphic frame multiplies a local section by a
holomorphic matrix, hence a smooth local section is **holomorphic** exactly when
its representatives in holomorphic frames are holomorphic functions. A
**Hermitian metric** $h$ on $E$ is a smooth bundle metric
([[def-smooth-bundle-metric]]) whose fibre pairings are positive definite
Hermitian forms, linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the
second; the condition is frame-independent because the gauge freedom is
conjugation by a pointwise invertible matrix. Smooth sections are
$\Gamma(E)$ ([[def-smooth-section-local-section-and-support]]).

derivations.claim: Define $S_d=S\oplus S^*$ and $R=U\oplus U^*$. On $S_d$ put $$\omega((s,\phi),(t,\psi))=\phi^Tt-\psi^Ts,\qquad J(s,\phi)=(H^{-1}\bar\phi,-H^T\bar s).$$ Then $\omega$ is a nondegenerate complex-bilinear alternating form, $J$ is antilinear, $J^2=-1$, and $\omega(Jx,Jy)=\overline{\omega(x,y)}$ by direct substitution and $H^\dagger=H$. Consequently $\omega(Jx,y)=-\overline{\omega(x,Jy)}$ and $h_d(Jx,Jy)=h_d(y,x)$. Thus $h_d(x,y)=\omega(x,Jy)$ is a nondegenerate first-slot-linear Hermitian form with matrix $\operatorname{diag}(H,H^{-T})$.

Fix $z
e0$ and write $A_z=\alpha(z)$, $B_z=\alpha(jz)$. On the real line spanned by $z,jz$, its linear coordinate $(a,b)$ gives $\alpha(a,b)=aA_z+bB_z$ and $ eta(a,b)=aB_z^\dagger H-bA_z^\dagger H$. Expanding $ eta(a,b)\alpha(a,b)=0$ in $a,b$ gives $A_z^\dagger HB_z=B_z^\dagger HA_z=0$ and $A_z^\dagger HA_z=B_z^\dagger HB_z=:G_z$. The matrix $G_z$ is invertible: if $G_zv=0$ for $v
e0$, injectivity of $A_z$ gives $A_zv
e0$, while $ eta(a,b)A_zv=0$ for every $(a,b)$. Its class is a global section of the trivial bundle $F_M|_\ell$ vanishing at $(1,0)$, hence is identically zero; exactness on $\ell$ would then put the constant $A_zv$ in the image of $H^0(U\otimes\mathcal O_\ell(-1))=0$, a contradiction by [F2].

Define $a_d(z)=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha(z),\beta(z)^T):R\to S_d$ and the complex-linear map $\Phi:R\otimes\mathbb C^4\to S_d$ by $\Phi(r\otimes z)=a_d(z)r$. Let $c(u,\phi)=(\bar\phi,\bar u)$, the antilinear involution of $R$. The two identities for $\beta$ give $J a_d(z)=a_d(jz)c$. Also $\operatorname{im}a_d(z)$ is $\omega$-isotropic, since its pairing is the transpose of $\beta(z)\alpha(z)=0$. Consequently $\mathscr H=\Phi^*h_d$ satisfies $\mathscr H((c\otimes j)x,(c\otimes j)y)=\mathscr H(y,x)$ and $R\otimes z\perp_{\mathscr H}R\otimes jz$.

The two images $\operatorname{im}A_z$ and $\operatorname{im}B_z$ are therefore nondegenerate and $H$-orthogonal. Their orthogonal complement $$E_z=\ker(A_z^\dagger H)\cap\ker(B_z^\dagger H)$$ is the section space of $F_M|_\ell$: in bases given by $A_z,B_z$ and $G_z^{-1}$, the first two summands form copies of the exact Euler complex $\mathcal O(-1)\to\mathcal O^2\to\mathcal O(1)$, and the remaining summand is $E_z\otimes\mathcal O$. Thus $H|_{E_z}$ is positive by [F1]. The doubled target complement is $E_z\oplus E_z^*$, on which $h_d$ is positive.

The form $\mathscr H$ is nondegenerate on $R\otimes z$ because its Gram matrix there is $\operatorname{diag}(G_z,G_z^T)$. Its orthogonal complement to $(R\otimes z)\oplus(R\otimes jz)$ maps by $\Phi$ into $E_z\oplus E_z^*$; hence $\mathscr H$ is nonnegative on that complement, with $\ker\Phi$ allowed. Moreover $\Phi$ is onto: the images of the $\alpha_i$ span $M$ by definition, and the annihilator of the span of the $\beta_i^T$ is $\bigcap_i\ker\beta_i=H^0(F_M)=0$ by [F1]. This verifies the linewise orthogonality, nondegeneracy, and complement-positivity hypotheses needed for the following finite matrix calculation.

Use the original middle space $S=M$ and its constant Hermitian matrix $H$, rather than the doubled coefficient space, for the remaining positivity calculation. Put $z_1=x_1+ix_2$, $z_2=x_3+ix_4$ and $$a(x)=\alpha(1,0,z_1,z_2)=a_0+z_1M_1+z_2M_2,\qquad b(x)=\alpha(0,1,-\bar z_2,\bar z_1)=b_0-\bar z_2M_1+\bar z_1M_2.$$ The two arguments are $z,jz$ in the stated coordinate convention. Step 1.2 gives $$a^\dagger Ha=b^\dagger Hb=A(x),\qquad a^\dagger Hb=0,$$ with $A(x)$ invertible for every $x$. Apply the same identities on the infinity line with $z=(0,0,1,0)$ and $jz=(0,0,0,1)$ to obtain $$M_1^\dagger HM_1=M_2^\dagger HM_2=C,\qquad M_1^\dagger HM_2=0,$$ where $C$ is invertible. Neither $A(x)$ nor $C$ is yet assumed positive. Let $K=A^{-1}$ and $$Q=1-aKa^\dagger H-bKb^\dagger H.$$ The Gram identities imply $Q^2=Q$ and $Q^\dagger H=HQ$; its range is precisely the real-line section complement $E_z$ in step 2.2. Thus $y^\dagger HQy=(Qy)^\dagger H(Qy)\ge0$ for every $y$, by the actual induced section pairing there. This identification uses the lifted identity $\beta=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H$ and the Euler-complex decomposition of step 2.2; it is not an extra assumption of positivity of $H$ on the coefficient images.

Put $P=a^\dagger HM_1$ and $R=a^\dagger HM_2$. Differentiating $a^\dagger Hb=0$ in $x_1,x_3$ gives $a^\dagger HM_2=-M_1^\dagger Hb$ and $a^\dagger HM_1=M_2^\dagger Hb$, hence $b^\dagger HM_1=-R^\dagger$ and $b^\dagger HM_2=P^\dagger$. Since $a_\mu=(M_1,iM_1,M_2,iM_2)$, the derivatives of $A$ are $$A_1=P+P^\dagger,\quad A_2=iP-iP^\dagger,\quad A_3=R+R^\dagger,\quad A_4=iR-iR^\dagger.$$ Pairing the real and imaginary derivatives, with the matrix order retained, gives $$\sum_\mu A_\mu K A_\mu =2(PKP^\dagger+P^\dagger KP+RKR^\dagger+R^\dagger KR) =\sum_\mu a_\mu^\dagger H(1-Q)a_\mu.$$ The second equality follows by substituting $1-Q=aKa^\dagger H+bKb^\dagger H$ and the displayed formulas for $b^\dagger HM_i$. As $\sum_\mu a_\mu^\dagger Ha_\mu=4C$, set $$D=\sum_\mu a_\mu^\dagger HQa_\mu =\sum_\mu(Qa_\mu)^\dagger H(Qa_\mu)\succeq0; \qquad \sum_\mu A_\mu K A_\mu=4C-D.$$ Also $\Delta A=2\sum_\mu a_\mu^\dagger Ha_\mu=8C$. Differentiating $AK=1$ twice therefore yields $$\Delta K=2K\Big(\sum_\mu A_\mu K A_\mu\Big)K-K(\Delta A)K =-2KDK\preceq0.$$ This last inequality is congruence by the Hermitian matrix $K$, and does not assume its positivity. Thus for every constant $v\in U$, $f_v(x)=v^\dagger K(x)v$ is a real smooth function with $\Delta f_v\le0$ on all of $\mathbb R^4$.

Expanding the Gram gives $A(x)=|x|^2C+O(|x|)$ uniformly in direction. Since $C$ is invertible, writing $A=r^2(C+E_r)$ with $\|E_r\|=O(r^{-1})$ and using the convergent geometric series for $(1+C^{-1}E_r)^{-1}$ proves $\|K(x)\|\le2\|C^{-1}\|r^{-2}$ for all sufficiently large $r$. In particular $f_v$ tends uniformly to zero at infinity. On a closed ball of radius $R$, the function $f_v-\delta|x|^2$ has strictly negative Laplacian for $\delta>0$ and cannot attain a minimum in the interior, where its real Hessian would be positive semidefinite. Hence $f_v(x)\ge\min_{|y|=R}f_v(y)-\delta R^2$. First let $\delta\downarrow0$, then let $R\to\infty$ with $x$ fixed. The uniform decay proves $f_v(x)\ge0$. Thus $K$ is positive semidefinite; being Hermitian and invertible, it is positive definite, as is $A$. At any fixed $x$, the $H$-orthogonal direct decomposition $$S=\operatorname{im}a\oplus\operatorname{im}b\oplus\operatorname{range}Q$$ has positive Gram $A$ on its first two summands and the positive section form of step 2.2 on the third. Therefore $H$ is positive definite. If $U=0$, $Q=1$ and the section positivity already gives this conclusion directly; no inverse of a nonzero-dimensional Gram is needed. The preceding splitting lemma retains the positive constant flat summand separately. This proves the stated arbitrary-rank claim without a coefficient-span surjectivity assumption or a transpose Clifford identity.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $r\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, let
$X=\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)=(\mathbb C^{r+1}\setminus\{0\})/\mathbb C^\times$
with its standard quotient complex-manifold structure, and let $E\to X$ be a
holomorphic vector bundle of finite rank.
Write $\mathcal O(E)$ for its sheaf of holomorphic sections, and let
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ denote the $q$th right-derived global-sections group of an
abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$. For
$0\le q\le r$, let $\mathcal A^{0,q}(E)$ be the sheaf of smooth sections of
$\Lambda^{0,q}T^*X\otimes_{\mathbb C}E$, where $\Lambda^{0,q}T^*X$ is the
$q$th exterior power of the antiholomorphic cotangent subbundle. In a
holomorphic local frame of $E$,
define $\bar\partial_E$ by applying the scalar $\bar\partial$ to each
coefficient form; holomorphic transition matrices make this definition
independent of frame, and $\bar\partial_E^2=0$. Set
$\mathcal A^{0,q}(E)=0$ for $q>r$ and define
$$H^q_{\bar\partial}(X,E):=\frac{\ker\bigl(\bar\partial_E:\Gamma(X,\mathcal A^{0,q}(E))\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal A^{0,q+1}(E))\bigr)}{\operatorname{im}\bigl(\bar\partial_E:\Gamma(X,\mathcal A^{0,q-1}(E))\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal A^{0,q}(E))\bigr)},$$
where $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ denotes the group of sections of $\mathcal F$ over
$X$ and the denominator is zero for $q=0$. For every $q\ge0$, the canonical
comparison induced by the smooth Dolbeault resolution is an isomorphism
$$H^q(X,\mathcal O(E))\cong H^q_{\bar\partial}(X,E).$$
For the trivial line bundle $E=\mathcal O_X$ and $0\le r\le3$, this gives
$$H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=\mathbb C,\qquad H^q(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=0\quad(q>0).$$
The scalar cohomology conclusion is obtained by the direct Laurent–Čech
calculation on the standard projective cover; no GAGA theorem, Kähler Hodge
theorem in dimensions above one, or arbitrary-coherent projective vanishing is
assumed.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ carry the antiholomorphic coordinate involution $\sigma([\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2])=[-\bar\lambda_2:\bar\lambda_1:-\bar\mu_2:\bar\mu_1]$. A linear monad is a locally split exact complex at its ends
$$
\mathcal O(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal O\otimes S\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal O(1)\otimes U'
$$
with locally free middle cohomology $F=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$, where $U,S,U'$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces. For a degree-one matrix $P(z)$ put $P^\#(z)=P(jz)^\dagger$ and define the signed dual monad $D(M):(U')^*\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\xrightarrow{-\beta^\#}S^*\otimes\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\alpha^\#}U^*\otimes\mathcal O(1)$; its cohomology is denoted $D(F)$, and dualizing twice uses $(P^\#)^\#=-P$ and $D^2(M)=M$. By a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian self-pairing we mean an isomorphism $h_F:F\to D(F)$ that is linear in its first variable, conjugate-linear in its second, and fixed by this bidual operation. Assume $H^0(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$, $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ for every $q\ge0$, and $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-2))=0$ for $q=0,1,2$. For any two such monads, every holomorphic morphism of their middle cohomology bundles lifts to a unique constant chain map between the monads. In particular, for a monad with a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian self-pairing, the unique lift is a chain isomorphism with Hermitian middle map $H=H^\dagger$ and normalized identities
$$
\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H,\qquad \beta(jz)^\dagger=-H\alpha(z),
$$
where $j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$ and the end spaces are identified by the lifted pairing.

Assume full AC. Then the analytic sheaf cohomology of $\mathcal O(-1)$ vanishes in every degree on $\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$ for $1\le r\le3$. The analytic cohomology of $\mathcal O(-2)$ vanishes in every degree on $\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$ for $r=2,3$. In particular, $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ and $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-2))=0$ for $q=0,1,2$. This is an analytic deduction from the named scalar-cohomology supplier and does not identify algebraic and analytic cohomology by GAGA.

Let
$$
\mathcal O(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal O\otimes S\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal O(1)\otimes U'
$$
be a locally split linear monad on $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ with locally free middle cohomology $F$. Suppose a nondegenerate Hermitian form $H$ on $S$, linear in the first variable, satisfies $\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H$ for $j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. Assume $H^0(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$, $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ for every $q\ge0$, and $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(-1))=0$. Define $L=\bigcap_i\ker\beta_i\subseteq S$ and $M=\sum_i\operatorname{im}\alpha_i\subseteq S$, where $\alpha(z)=\sum_i z_i\alpha_i$ and $\beta(z)=\sum_i z_i\beta_i$. If the Hermitian form induced by $H$ on $H^0(F|_\ell)$ is positive definite for every $\sigma$-invariant real line $\ell$, then $H^0(F)=L=M^{\perp_H}$, $H|_L$ is positive definite, and $S=L\oplus M$ is an $H$-orthogonal decomposition. The monad and its pairing split as the constant summand $L\otimes\mathcal O$ plus the reduced monad $U\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to M\otimes\mathcal O\to U'\otimes\mathcal O(1)$; the reduced cohomology has no global sections and remains positive on every real line. The conclusion includes $U=0$, when $L=S$ and $M=0$.

Let $M$ be the coefficient-image subspace of a linear monad on $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ after removing its constant orthogonal summand as in the preceding splitting lemma. Thus its reduced middle cohomology has no global sections, is trivial on every $\sigma$-invariant real line, and has a positive section pairing on each such line. Let $H$ be the induced nondegenerate Hermitian form on $M$, linear in the first variable, and suppose $\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H$ and $\beta(z)\alpha(z)=0$ for every $z\in\mathbb C^4$, with $j^2=-1$. Then $H$ is positive definite on all of $M$.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, and let $B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$ satisfy $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Define for $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$
$$
a_z=(B_1-z_1,\ B_2-z_2,\ J)^T:V\to V\oplus V\oplus W,\qquad
b_z^\dagger=(-B_2+z_2,\ B_1-z_1,\ I):V\oplus V\oplus W\to V.
$$
Then $a_z$ is injective for every $z$ if and only if the datum is costable, and $b_z^\dagger$ is surjective for every $z$ if and only if the datum is stable, where stability and costability have their word-span and invariant-subspace meanings. For the homogeneous linear maps
$$
\alpha=(B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1,\ B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2,\ J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2)^T,
$$
$$
\beta=(-C,\ A,\ I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2),\quad
A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1,\quad
C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2,
$$
fiberwise injectivity of $\alpha$ and surjectivity of $\beta$ on $\mathbb P^3$ imply regularity. Conversely, if the datum is regular and both raw moment maps vanish, then these homogeneous maps are fiberwise injective and surjective and form a linear bundle monad.

Use the dual-number scheme, relative projective-space charts, finite locally free sheaves and twisting sheaves in [[def-dual-numbers-scheme]], [[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]], [[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]] and [[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]], with the inherited AC convention for the twisting-sheaf construction. Let $A=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ and equip it with the conjugate-linear involution $\overline{a+b\epsilon}=\bar a+\bar b\epsilon$. Its reduction is the quotient map $A\to\mathbb C$ sending $\epsilon$ to zero. For every $r\in\mathbb R$, the map $\rho_r:A\to A$ fixing $\mathbb C$ and sending $\epsilon$ to $r\epsilon$ preserves this involution.

A **first-order family of positive real linear monads of dimensions $(k,2k+N,k)$** is a three-term complex of locally free sheaves on $\mathbb P^3_A=\operatorname{Proj}A[\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2]$,
$$\mathcal O(-1)\otimes_A U_A\xrightarrow{\alpha_A}\mathcal O\otimes_A S_A\xrightarrow{\beta_A}\mathcal O(1)\otimes_A U'_A,$$
where $U_A,S_A,U'_A$ are free $A$-modules of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, each map is homogeneous linear in $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)$, $\beta_A\alpha_A=0$, $\alpha_A$ is a locally split injection, $\beta_A$ is a locally split surjection, and $F_A=\ker\beta_A/\operatorname{im}\alpha_A$ is locally free of rank $N$. The two short exact sequences defined by the kernel and image split locally; hence their formation and the middle cohomology commute with reduction $A\to\mathbb C$. The reduced complex is therefore an ordinary linear monad on $\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C$.

The **first-order locally-free/base-change range** used here further requires that $H^0(\mathbb P^3_A,F_A)$ is a free $A$-module and reduction identifies it with $H^0(\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C,F_0)$, where $F_0=F_A\otimes_A\mathbb C$. The image in $S_A$ of the map from the four coefficient copies of $U_A$ under $\alpha_A$ is a direct summand and reduces to the corresponding coefficient-image subspace of $S_0$. For each real twistor line $\ell$ in the reduced projective space, the restriction of $F_A$ to $\ell_A=\ell\times_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Spec}A$ is trivial of rank $N$, and reduction identifies its global sections with $H^0(\ell,F_0|_\ell)$. These conditions state the precise global, coefficient-image, and line-section base-change range; no arbitrary analytic family or algebraization assertion is included.

Extend the coordinate map $j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$ semilinearly using the involution of $A$; its projective action $\sigma$ is an involution and preserves each real twistor line. A **real twistor line** means the projectivization of a $j$-invariant complex two-plane in $\mathbb C^4$. Equivalently these are the finite lines
$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,\qquad (z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2,$$
together with $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Indeed a nonzero vector $v$ and $jv$ are complex-linearly independent because $j^2=-1$; they span the invariant plane. If its $\lambda$ projection is nonzero, that projection and its quaternionic conjugate give an invertible two-by-two matrix with determinant $|\lambda_1|^2+|\lambda_2|^2$, so it has exactly the displayed graph form; if the projection is zero the plane is the $\mu$ plane. Each fixed-line restriction above means the corresponding constant thickening $\ell_A$.

A first-order real structure on the monad is a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian pairing on $F_A$, linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, whose reduction induces a positive-definite Hermitian form on the holomorphic section space of every real line. A unitary framing at infinity is an isometric isomorphism $F_A|_{\ell_\infty}\cong (A\otimes_\mathbb C W)\otimes_A\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$, where $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ has its standard Hermitian form.

An isomorphism of such families is an $A$-linear chain isomorphism that intertwines the $\sigma$-Hermitian pairings and the framing. No order or positivity is assigned to elements of $A$ with nonzero nilpotent part: positivity is required only after reduction. The base-change scope in this definition consists exactly of reduction $\epsilon\mapsto0$ and the involution-preserving maps $\rho_r$ for real $r$.

Let $\mathcal F$ be the locally free algebraic middle cohomology of a linear monad
$$
\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(-1)^{\oplus k}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}^{\oplus(2k+N)}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1)^{\oplus k}
$$
on $\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C$, with exactness at both ends. Let $H_{\rm alg}=c_1^{\rm alg}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$ in the Chow ring and let $H_{\rm top}=c_1^{\rm top}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$ in singular cohomology. The hyperplane cycle map identifies $H_{\rm alg}$ with $H_{\rm top}$; write $H$ for either class in the corresponding formula. The algebraic Chern character is $N-kH_{\rm alg}^2$, the algebraic first Chern class is zero, the algebraic second Chern class is $kH_{\rm alg}^2$, and the algebraic Euler characteristic is $N-2k$. The underlying topological bundle has total Chern class $1+kH_{\rm top}^2$ through degree six and topological Chern character $N-kH_{\rm top}^2$.

Identify $\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C$ with the twistor space of $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ by the quaternionic structure whose invariant lines are the real incidence lines in the positive stereographic coordinates. Let $\pi:\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C\to S^4$ be the resulting fibration, orient each fiber by its complex orientation, orient the base so the incidence chart followed by the fiber orientation gives the complex orientation of $\mathbb P^3$, and let $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ be the positive point class. Then $\pi^*u=H^2$. Consequently, if the underlying topological bundle of $\mathcal F$ is $\pi^*E$ for a rank-$N$ complex bundle $E\to S^4$ with $c_1(E)=0$, then $c_2(E)=ku$ and $\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=k$.

Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, standard Hermitian $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ and ADHM data $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with the complex equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Stability means that the $B_1,B_2$ words applied to $I(W)$ span $V$; costability means no nonzero common invariant subspace of $V$ lies in $\ker J$; regular means both. Set

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

For every $\zeta>0$, each stable $GL(V)$ orbit meets $\mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V$ in exactly one $U(V)$ orbit, and the inclusion induces a diffeomorphism of smooth real manifolds

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^s/GL(V).$$

At $\zeta=0$, every stable datum satisfying the real equation is automatically costable. Each regular complex orbit meets the zero real level in exactly one unitary orbit, giving instead

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=0,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V).$$

Both identifications are equivariant for the compact rotation/framing torus in the raw-data convention. For $k=0$ all spaces are points. This theorem identifies the stated finite-dimensional quotients; it asserts no correspondence with sheaves or ASD connections, and no identification of the entire positive-FI quotient with the zero-FI regular locus.

For $r\ge1$, let $H=\{[Z_0:\cdots:Z_r]\in\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C):Z_0=0\}$ and
let $i:H\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$ be inclusion. For every
integer $m$, the homogeneous coordinate $Z_0$ defines an exact sequence of
holomorphic sheaves
$$
0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(m-1)
\xrightarrow{\ \cdot Z_0\ }\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(m)
\longrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_H(m)\longrightarrow0.
$$
Here $i_*\mathcal O_H(m)$ assigns to an open set $U$ the holomorphic
sections of $\mathcal O_H(m)$ on $U\cap H$. Twisting the sequence with
$m=0$ by $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(-1)$ gives, in particular,
$$
0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(-2)
\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(-1)
\longrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_H(-1)\longrightarrow0.
$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring with $1$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]), let $n\ge0$, let $d\in\mathbb Z$ and
let $X=\mathbb P^n_A\cong\operatorname{Proj}A[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be relative
projective space ([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]],
[[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]), with twisting sheaf
$\mathcal O_X(d)$ ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]]) and cohomology
$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$. Then
$$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0\qquad\text{unless }q=0\text{ or }q=n.$$
If $n>0$, then $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ when $d\ge0$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0$ when $d<0$, where
$A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ is the degree-$d$ graded piece
([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]); and $H^n(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ is the
free $A$-module on the Laurent monomials $x_0^{e_0}\cdots x_n^{e_n}$ with
$e_i<0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_ie_i=d$, so that it is nonzero precisely when
$d\le-n-1$ and $A\ne0$. For $n=0$ one has $\mathbb P^0_A=\operatorname{Spec}A$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A$ for every $d\in\mathbb Z$, with all higher
groups zero. The zero ring $A=0$ is allowed: then $X=\varnothing$ and all
groups are zero, in agreement with both displayed descriptions.

derivations.claim: First the holomorphic monad maps have homogeneous linear entries. Indeed, in the $m=1$ sequence of [F10], $H^1(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=0$ by [A1], so restriction $H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O(1))\to H^0(\mathbb P^{r-1},\mathcal O(1))$ is surjective and its kernel is the defining hyperplane coordinate times $H^0(\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$. Starting with $r=0$, where $\mathcal O(1)$ on a point has one-dimensional section space, induction shows that every section is a linear combination of the homogeneous coordinates: subtract the global coordinate lifts of its restriction, then the remaining section is a constant multiple of the defining coordinate. This applies to entries of both $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O(-1),\mathcal O)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O,\mathcal O(1))$. Thus no algebraic/analytic comparison is needed to introduce their four coefficient maps. By [A1] and [F9], the hyperplane sequences and analytic scalar theorem give exactly the negative-twist vanishings required by [F1]. Apply [F1] to the pairing isomorphism; it gives the unique constant Hermitian lift $H$ with the signed identities there. Thus no algebraic cohomology group is being substituted for the analytic lifting groups.

For the algebraic $\mathbb P^3_A=\operatorname{Proj}A[\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2]$ family category, [F11] directly supplies the needed $\mathcal O(-1)$ and $\mathcal O(-2)$ groups over $A$ and $H^0(\mathcal O_A)=A$. Separately, on the analytic first-order thickening each twist has the split underlying analytic sheaf $\mathcal O_A(d)=\mathcal O(d)\oplus\epsilon\mathcal O(d)$; finite direct sums commute with sheaf cohomology, so [F9] gives the same vanishings there. Thus a holomorphic family pairing can be lifted analytically, whereas algebraic family sheaves use [F11]; neither computation substitutes algebraic cohomology for an analytic group or invokes GAGA. Both yield constant $A$-valued chain maps. In both categories the two kernel/image sequences identify global sections with the same constant coefficient kernel of $\beta_A$, so the specified global-section base-change condition is respected by this identification. Repeating the obstruction and ambiguity calculation of [F1] over these coefficient modules lifts the family pairing uniquely to an $A$-linear constant chain isomorphism with Hermitian middle matrix $H_A$; its inverse exists because its reduction is invertible. Global section base change identifies $H^0(F_A)$ with the constant coefficient kernel $L_A$ in $S_A$. Its reduction is injective, so a full-rank minor is a unit and $L_A$ is a direct summand.

By [F2], the global constant subspace $L$ is positive and $S=L\oplus M$ orthogonally, and the reduced monad on $M$ preserves the full framing. Apply [F3] to that reduced monad; it proves $H|_M$ positive. Since $H|_L$ is positive and the sum is orthogonal, $H$ is positive definite on all of $S$. In particular the argument also covers $k=0$, where $M=0$.

By hypothesis the coefficient-image module $M_A$ is a direct summand. The coefficient identities give $M_A^\perp=L_A$; for a direct summand in a finite free module with a perfect pairing, the restriction map to its dual is split-surjective, so taking orthogonal complements twice returns that summand. Hence $M_A=L_A^\perp$ and $S_A=L_A\oplus M_A$. The line-section base change and the vanishing $H^0(\ell_A,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ make restriction of $L_A$ injective; the reduced line positivity makes $H_A|_{L_0}$ positive. The internal-positivity proof applies to the reduction on $M_0$, so its reduced form is positive too. On infinity the family framing identifies the remaining orthogonal complement isometrically with $W_A$.

Write the four coefficient maps of $\alpha$ as $P=\alpha_{\lambda_1}$, $Q=\alpha_{\lambda_2}$, $R=\alpha_{\mu_1}$, and $T=\alpha_{\mu_2}$. From the first-slot convention and $j^2=-1$, the corresponding coefficients of $\beta$ are $Q^\dagger H,-P^\dagger H,T^\dagger H,-R^\dagger H$ in that order. The $\mu_1^2,\mu_2^2,\mu_1\mu_2$ coefficients of $\beta\alpha=0$ give $T^\dagger HR=R^\dagger HT=0$ and $R^\dagger HR=T^\dagger HT$. The maps $R,T$ are injective by exactness at the two coordinate points of $\ell_\infty$. Positivity of $H$ therefore makes their common Gram matrix $G$ positive definite. Replacing the paired end bases by $G^{-1/2}$ normalizes both maps to isometries with orthogonal images. Choosing an orthonormal basis of $S$ then identifies $R=-\iota_1$, $T=-\iota_2$ and $S=(V\oplus V)\oplus W_0$, with $W_0$ their orthogonal complement.

At infinity the maps are $\alpha_\infty=-\mu_1\iota_1-\mu_2\iota_2$ and $\beta_\infty=\mu_2\iota_1^\dagger-\mu_1\iota_2^\dagger$. For every $[\mu_1:\mu_2]\in\mathbb P^1$, the kernel of $\beta_\infty$ in $V\oplus V$ is the line-valued copy $\{(\mu_1v,\mu_2v):v\in V\}$, which is exactly the image of $\alpha_\infty$; $W_0$ is killed by $\beta_\infty$ and meets that image trivially. Therefore the restricted cohomology and its section pairing are canonically $W_0\otimes\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$ and its standard positive form. The specified unitary framing identifies $W_0$ with $W$ without discarding any flat summand.

Relative to $S=V\oplus V\oplus W$, write $P=(B_1,B_2,J)^T$ and $Q=(Q_1,Q_2,Q_W)^T$. The coefficient of $\lambda_1\mu_1$ in $\beta\alpha=0$ is $Q^\dagger HR+T^\dagger HP=0$, so $Q_1=-B_2^\dagger$; the coefficient of $\lambda_1\mu_2$ is $Q^\dagger HT-R^\dagger HP=0$, so $Q_2=B_1^\dagger$. Define $I^\dagger=Q_W$. These definitions give exactly the displayed $\alpha$ and, by the lifted reality identity, the displayed $\beta$.

The $\lambda_1^2$ coefficient of $\beta\alpha=0$ is $Q^\dagger HP=0$. Substitution of the blocks gives $-[B_2,B_1]+IJ=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. The $\lambda_1\lambda_2$ coefficient is $Q^\dagger HQ-P^\dagger HP=0$. Expanding it gives $[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0$, which is $\mu_{\mathbb R}=0$. Conversely, these two moment equations make all coefficients of $\beta\alpha$ vanish, and direct substitution yields $$\beta\alpha=\lambda_1^2\mu_{\mathbb C} +\lambda_1\lambda_2\mu_{\mathbb R} -\lambda_2^2\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger=0.$$

Let a normalized framed chain isomorphism have domain, middle and target maps $g_-,g_0,g_+$. It preserves $H$, so $g_0$ is unitary. Comparing the two $\mu$ coefficients forces $g_0|_{V\oplus0}=g_-$ and $g_0|_{0\oplus V}=g_-$; unitarity then preserves $W_0$. The infinity framing is fixed, so $g_0|_{W_0}=1$. Thus $g_0=\operatorname{diag}(g,g,1)$ for one $g\in U(V)$, and the $\lambda$ coefficients force $B_i'=gB_ig^{-1}$, $I'=gI$, and $J'=Jg^{-1}$. Surjectivity of $\beta$ makes $g_+$ uniquely determined and equal to $g$. Conversely, each such $g$ defines the displayed pairing-preserving framed chain isomorphism. Hence there are no residual transformations beyond simultaneous $U(V)$.

On the affine chart $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2] =[1:0:z_1:z_2]$, the raw maps are $a_z$ and $b_z^\dagger$ from [F5]. Since the original $\alpha,\beta$ have their required ranks at every point, [F5] gives costability and stability. Thus the extracted zero-moment datum is regular. Conversely, for stable and costable data, [F5] proves full homogeneous rank, composition zero, and local splitting, so the raw formula does define the required monad.

Put $B_1'=t_1B_1$, $B_2'=t_2B_2$, $I'=Ih^{-1}$, and $J'=t_1t_2hJ$. Substituting $(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ into the primed $A,C$ gives $A'=t_1A$ and $C'=t_2C$. Substitution into $\alpha'$ then gives $$\alpha'(g_tz)(t_1t_2)^{-1} =\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)\alpha(z).$$ The same substitution into $\beta'$ gives $\beta'(g_tz)\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)=\beta(z)$. The factors therefore are the stated chain maps; on the framed flavor coordinates $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_a^{-1})$ supplies the stated weights.

After lifting reduced orthonormal bases, the common Gram matrix of the two $\mu$ coefficient maps has the form $I+\epsilon K$ with $K=K^\dagger$. The change $T=I-\tfrac12\epsilon K$ satisfies $T^\dagger(I+\epsilon K)T=I$ using $\epsilon^2=0$ and $\bar\epsilon=\epsilon$. This normalizes both $\mu$ maps over $A$ without ordering nilpotent elements or asserting nilpotent positivity. Choices of lifted normalized bases differ by the residual $U(k,A)$ action proved in step 5.2, so coefficient extraction is independent of those choices on isomorphism classes.

For any such raw datum and finite $z$, write $a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T$ and $b_z^\dagger=(-B_2+z_2,B_1-z_1,I)$. The two moment equations give $b_z^\dagger a_z=0$ and $a_z^\dagger a_z=b_z^\dagger b_z=:f_z$. Regularity makes both maps full rank, so $f_z$ is positive definite. On $\ell_z$ the monad is $\alpha=a_z\lambda_1+b_z\lambda_2$ and $\beta=b_z^\dagger\lambda_1-a_z^\dagger\lambda_2$. The cross Gram terms vanish, and $a_z,b_z$ identify two orthogonal copies of $V$ after applying $f_z^{-1/2}$. In these orthonormal coordinates the end maps on the first two copies are $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)^T$ and $(-\lambda_2,\lambda_1)$, the Euler complex $V\mathcal O(-1)\to(V\oplus V)\mathcal O\to V\mathcal O(1)$; the complementary term is $E_z\mathcal O$. Hence $H^0(F|_{\ell_z})=E_z$ with its positive induced form, and $F|_{\ell_z}$ is trivial. At infinity the same calculation in step 4.1 gives $W\otimes\mathcal O$ and its framing. The maps in step 6.1 are exactly the required locally split end maps.

The zero-level quotient result [F8] applies because step 6.1 established stability and both zero moments; it identifies each regular complex orbit with its unique unitary orbit. The explicit argument in step 5.2 is stronger for the framed real monads: it identifies their actual normalized isomorphisms with $U(V)$ and fixes the inverse extraction orbit. If a constant flat summand is present, [F2] places it in the framed $W_0$ complement and the same fixed-frame argument leaves it unchanged. When $k=0$, every map into or out of $V=0$ is zero and $U(0)$ has one element. Because all coefficient images lie in $M=L^\perp$, $J$ has no component in the framed flat subspace $L\subset W$ and $I$ vanishes on that subspace. Thus flat directions remain as unused directions of $W$.

The coefficient equations in steps 4.2 and 5.1 are polynomial identities, so over $A$ they give the same block form and both moment equations. Conversely, take an $A$-valued zero-moment datum whose reduction is regular. Every full-rank minor of its reduced raw maps lifts to a unit in the local rings of the first-order thickening; thus the end maps are locally split and the cohomology is locally free. On a fixed real line the matrices $a_z,b_z$ have full-rank reductions, so their common Gram $f_z$ is invertible over $A$. Their orthogonal images split off two free copies of $V_A$, leaving a free rank-$N$ complement; the line complex is the Euler complex plus that constant complement, so its sections commute with reduction. The global section and coefficient-image conditions are exactly the additional range conditions imposed in the Statement. The standard middle form induces a nondegenerate real pairing, positive after reduction. Thus such data give families in the stated range. The proof of step 5.2 uses only coefficient comparison, the framing, and $g^\dagger g=1$, so it gives exactly $U(k,A)$ as the residual group. Reduction and each map $\epsilon\mapsto r\epsilon$ commute with coefficient extraction and with the correction $T$. This proves first-order naturality for precisely the stated base changes.

The finite monad resolution and its locally free cohomology give the algebraic Chern character and Chern classes in [F7]. Its same finite line resolution yields the topological classes after the hyperplane cycle class is identified with the Euler class of the complex normal line. The positive incidence-fiber Thom calculation in [F7] gives $\pi^*u=H_{\rm top}^2$. If the topological bundle is $\pi^*E$, naturality gives $\pi^*c_2(E)=kH_{\rm top}^2=k\pi^*u$; since $\pi^*u$ is a generator, $c_2(E)=ku$. This is conditional on the pullback hypothesis and asserts no Ward correspondence.
